newsitem.title: ZAIRE: EU won't recognise Zaire rebel authority - envoy.
newsitem.headline: EU won't recognise Zaire rebel authority - envoy.

text.p: European Union envoy Aldo Ajello said on Monday Europe could not recognise the authority of Rwandan-backed Zairean rebels who have taken over a strip along the eastern frontier.
He also suggested that a planned international force for Zaire should have the mandate to help the government to reassert its authority in the area.
"We do not recognise any authority in Kivu (Province) which is not the Zaire government," Ajello told a news conference in the Zaire capital.
"The most basic of issues and the reason why I'm here today is to permit Zaire to recover total sovereignty over its territory as rapidly as possible."

Ajello said he favoured giving a political dimension to the multinational force in line with what the Kinshasa government wants, to try and resolve the crisis rather than just providing humanitarian assistance for the refugees.

"We still need an international force for humanitarian reasons but also a force whose mission should be expanded to include a mandate that not only allows it to deal with the effects but also with the causes," Ajello said.

Ajello said there were divisions within Laurent Kabila's rebel group between ethnic Banyamulenge (Tutsis) who are fighting for citizenship within Zaire and Kabila himself who wants to conquer the country.
